subtitle: A king famed for justice faces the one decision his own chronicler could not cleanse.

panels.shot: wide, split-composition: Sher Shah on one rampart, Puran Mal on another, Raisen fort between them under stormy skies
panels.action: Sher Shah Suri stands stern atop a Mughal-style encampment ridge, while Puran Mal, proud Rajput lord of Raisen, grips his sword on the fort walls; dark clouds coil above the ancient hill-fort.

dialogue.text: In 1543 at Raisen, Sher Shah Suri swore safe passage to Puran Mal—and his own admiring chronicler then recorded how that oath ended in massacre.

i18n.hi: १५४३ में रायसेन पर, शेरशाह सूरी ने पुरन मल को सलामत राह का वचन दिया — और उसके मुरीद इतिहासकार ने ही लिखा कि वो वचन कत्लेआम पर ख़त्म हुआ।

panels.shot: slow push-in on Sher Shah in his command tent, maps and farman scrolls around him
panels.action: Sher Shah Suri sits in his campaign tent, hand resting on a map marked with roads and forts, his face calm yet hardened by years of war and rule.

dialogue.text: By 1543, Sher Shah Suri was famed for straight roads, fair revenue, and swift justice. Yet his armies still moved, and Raisen lay outside his order.

i18n.hi: १५४३ तक शेरशाह सीधे रास्तों, ठीक लगान और तेज़ इंसाफ़ के लिए मशहूर था। पर उसकी फ़ौजें चलती रहीं, और रायसेन अभी उसके क़ायदे से बाहर था।

panels.shot: medium on Puran Mal atop Raisen’s stone battlements, overlooking rugged countryside
panels.action: Puran Mal stands on the high stone ramparts of Raisen fort, hand on the hilt of his sword, gazing down at the plains where dust from advancing troops rises.

dialogue.text: Raisen’s lord, Puran Mal, held a hill-fort near Bhopal. For Sher Shah, it was a Rajput stronghold he could not ignore on the road that bound his empire.

i18n.hi: रायसेन के मालिक पुरन मल के पास भोपाल के पास पहाड़ी क़िला था। शेरशाह के लिए वो राजपूत गढ़ था, जिसे वो अपने साम्राज्य वाली राह पर नज़रअंदाज़ नहीं कर सकता था।

panels.shot: epic bird’s-eye of the Sur camp ringed around Raisen, siege lines snaking
panels.action: From above, the Sur imperial camp rings the hill of Raisen; tents, artillery and war-elephants encircle the fort as smoke from cooking fires coils into the dusk.

dialogue.text: Abbas Khan Sarwani, Sher Shah’s own chronicler, tells how the Sur army encircled Raisen. Cannons were placed, trenches dug, the fort shut off from the world.

i18n.hi: शेरशाह के अपने इतिहासकार अब्बास ख़ान सरवानी लिखते हैं कि सूर फ़ौज ने रायसेन को घेर लिया। तोपें जमीं, खाइयाँ खोदी गईं, क़िला दुनिया से काट दिया गया।

panels.shot: low-angle from inside Raisen, defenders and families huddled in courtyards
panels.action: Inside the stone-walled courtyard, Rajput soldiers stand tense while women and children cluster behind carved pillars, eyes lifted as distant cannon smoke drifts over the walls.

dialogue.text: Days of siege weighed on Raisen. Food shrank, fear grew. Puran Mal’s garrison stood with their families behind heavy gates, knowing Sher Shah’s reputation—and his power.

i18n.hi: दिनों की घेराबंदी ने रायसेन को दबा दिया। राशन घटा, ख़ौफ़ बढ़ा। पुरन मल की टुकड़ी अपने उरोजों के साथ भारी फाटकों के पीछे खड़ी थी, शेरशाह की शोहरत — और ताकत — दोनों जानती हुई।

panels.shot: close three-quarter view of Sher Shah on a rampart of his camp, gesturing toward the fort
panels.action: Sher Shah, armored but bareheaded, stands on an earthen rampart; he extends an open palm toward Raisen, face composed like a judge weighing a case.

dialogue.text: Sarwani writes that Sher Shah preferred terms to needless slaughter. From the siege lines, envoys rode with offers, hoping Raisen would bend without breaking.

i18n.hi: सरवानी लिखते हैं, शेरशाह बेमतलब खून से ज़्यादा सुलह पसंद करता था। घेरा छोड़कर वज़ीर शर्तें लेकर गए, उम्मीद थी रायसेन झुकेगा, टूटेगा नहीं।

panels.shot: tight interior scene, Puran Mal in council with his nobles, lamp-lit faces
panels.action: In a dim chamber within Raisen, Puran Mal leans over a low table as Rajput nobles sit around him, lamplight catching their anxious eyes and the steel of their ornaments.

dialogue.text: “If the Sur king swears on God, can we trust his word?”

i18n.hi: “अगर सूर बादशाह ख़ुदा की क़सम खाए, क्या उसके लफ़्ज़ पर भरोसा किया जाए?”

panels.shot: medium on Sher Shah and envoys facing each other in open field, hands raised solemnly
panels.action: Between fort and camp, Sher Shah stands flanked by commanders, right hand lifted in oath, while emissaries from Raisen listen, their faces a mix of doubt and hope.

dialogue.text: According to Sarwani, Sher Shah swore a solemn promise: safe passage for Puran Mal, his family, and retinue if they surrendered Raisen and left his territory.

i18n.hi: सरवानी के मुताबिक़ शेरशाह ने सख़्त वचन दिया: अगर रायसेन छोड़कर उसका इलाक़ा खाली कर दें, तो पुरन मल, उसके उरोजों और साथियों को सलामत राह मिलेगी।

panels.shot: dramatic close-up on Puran Mal’s face as he looks from fort walls toward the Sur camp
panels.action: Puran Mal stands at the gateway, watching the distant figure of Sher Shah; his jaw tightens, but a glimmer of relief touches his eyes as he lowers his sword.

dialogue.text: The chronicler says Puran Mal accepted. Raisen’s gates would open. In return, the Rajput lord staked everything on the Sur king’s sworn word.

i18n.hi: इतिहासकार कहता है, पुरन मल मान गया। रायसेन के फाटक खुलने वाले थे। बदले में उस राजपूत सरदार ने अपना सब कुछ सूर बादशाह के क़सम खाए लफ़्ज़ पर रख दिया।

panels.shot: wide moving column shot: Puran Mal’s people leaving the fort, carts, horses, slow procession
panels.action: A long, somber column winds down from Raisen’s gate—warriors on horseback, women on palanquins, children on ox-carts—moving under the watchful eyes of Sur soldiers.

dialogue.text: Sarwani describes them leaving the fort under truce, guarded by Sur troops. It was the fragile, dangerous moment when surrender relied only on trust.

i18n.hi: सरवानी बताते हैं, वो लोग सुलह के ताबे क़िले से निकले, सूर सिपाहियों की निगरानी में। ये वही नाज़ुक, ख़तरनाक पल था, जब समर्पण का सहारा बस भरोसा था।

panels.shot: interior camp scene, close on a group of Muslim survivors pleading before Sher Shah
panels.action: In Sher Shah’s tent, a group of weary, plainly dressed men and women kneel, their faces marked by hardship, hands lifted in appeal toward the seated king.

dialogue.text: Then Sarwani’s story turns. Muslim survivors from Chanderi came before Sher Shah, accusing Puran Mal of having earlier enslaved and abused them.

i18n.hi: फिर सरवानी की दास्तान पलट जाती है। चंदेरी के बचे हुए मुसलमान शेरशाह के सामने आए, इल्ज़ाम लगाया कि पुरन मल ने पहले उन्हें ग़ुलाम बनाया और सताया था।

panels.shot: tight, conflicted close-up on Sher Shah’s face, shadow cutting across
panels.action: Sher Shah sits rigid, half his face in shadow; his eyes burn with anger, but his hand still rests near a scroll—a silent reminder of his recent oath.

dialogue.text: Sarwani reports their words stirred Sher Shah’s fury. Justice for the oppressed stood against the oath just sworn. In that tension, the king had to choose.

i18n.hi: सरवानी लिखते हैं, उनके लफ़्ज़ों ने शेरशाह का ग़ुस्सा भड़का दिया। मज़लूमों का इंसाफ़, अभी‑अभी खाई गई क़सम के सामने खड़ा था। उसी टकराव में बादशाह को चुनना था।

panels.shot: medium shot of Sher Shah issuing orders to Isa Khan Niazi, finger pointing toward the departing column
panels.action: Outside the tent, Sher Shah faces his commander Isa Khan Niazi, arm extended toward the distant line of departing Raisen folk, while Isa stands attentive, hand on his sword-hilt.

dialogue.text: Sarwani says Sher Shah ordered Isa Khan Niazi to pursue Puran Mal’s column and destroy it. The safe-conduct was set aside; the oath was broken.

i18n.hi: सरवानी कहते हैं, शेरशाह ने ईसा ख़ान नियाज़ी को हुक्म दिया कि पुरन मल के काफ़िले का पीछा करके उसे मिटा दे। अमाननामे को किनारे रख दिया गया; वचन टूट गया।

panels.shot: tense long shot: Isa Khan’s cavalry bearing down on the marching column at a distance
panels.action: Across open scrubland, horsemen under Isa Khan gallop in formation toward the slower column of Puran Mal’s people, dust plumes merging as they draw near.

dialogue.text: No body counts are given. But Sarwani is clear: Isa Khan’s men overtook them, and the garrison and families who had trusted the oath were destroyed.

i18n.hi: लाशों की गिनती नहीं मिलती। पर सरवानी साफ़ लिखते हैं: ईसा ख़ान के लोग उन्हें जा लिए, और वो टुकड़ी और उरोजे जो वचन पर भरोसा करके चले थे, मिटा दी गई।

panels.shot: somber mid-shot: Puran Mal in the midst of chaos, turning decisively toward his kin
panels.action: In a chaotic field, Puran Mal stands amid fleeing figures and advancing horsemen; he turns back toward his kin, eyes fierce, lifting his sword in a grim resolve.

dialogue.text: Rajput memory, as studied by modern historians, would later shape this moment into heroic last stands and tragic choices. But the core fact remains: the surrendered column was attacked.

i18n.hi: राजपूत यादें, जिन्हें आज के इतिहासकारों ने पढ़ा, बाद में इस लम्हे को बहादुर आख़िरी जंग और दर्दनाक फ़ैसले की शक्ल देती हैं। मगर मूल बात साफ़ है: समर्पण कर चुका काफ़िला ही निशाना बना।

panels.shot: wide aftermath shot: empty field with abandoned belongings, Raisen fort looming far behind
panels.action: After the attack, the field lies quiet; overturned carts, dropped veils and broken shields scatter the ground, while Raisen’s silhouette rises far behind in harsh sunlight.

dialogue.text: K.R. Qanungo and Satish Chandra read Sarwani’s account plainly: Sher Shah violated terms he had sworn. Raisen became the dark exception to his fame for justice.

i18n.hi: के.आर. क़ानूंगो और सतीश चंद्र ने सरवानी की बात सीधी तरह से पढ़ी: शेरशाह ने अपने खाए हुए वचन की शर्त तोड़ी। रायसेन, उसके इंसाफ़ की शोहरत पर पड़ा काला धब्बा बन गया।

panels.shot: reflective mid-shot: Sher Shah alone on a ridge at dusk, looking toward Raisen
panels.action: At dusk, Sher Shah stands alone on a ridge, turbaned head bowed as he looks toward the now-quiet fort of Raisen, the sky stained orange and purple above him.

dialogue.text: Sarwani, loyal to Sher Shah, still records the broken promise and massacre. He does not excuse it; he preserves it as part of the king’s real reign.

i18n.hi: शेरशाह के वफ़ादार सरवानी फिर भी टूटा वादा और कत्लेआम लिखते हैं। वो उसे माफ़ नहीं करते; उसे बादशाह की असली हुकूमत का हिस्सा करके रख देते हैं।

panels.shot: conceptual split shot: one half showing Sher Shah’s road and sarai, other half Raisen’s desolate hill
panels.action: The scene divides visually: on one side, a busy metalled road with travelers and a sarai built under Sher Shah; on the other, Raisen’s lonely hill-fort under brooding clouds.

dialogue.text: Thus Sher Shah’s legacy holds both: ordered roads, reformed revenues, and also Raisen—a place where royal justice met anger and broke its own word.

i18n.hi: इस तरह शेरशाह की विरासत में दोनों हैं: तरतीबदार सड़कें, सुधरे हुए महसूल — और रायसेन भी, जहाँ शाहाना इंसाफ़ ग़ुस्से से टकराकर अपने ही लफ़्ज़ से फिर गया।

panels.shot: extreme close-up on an unseen narrator’s weathered hand closing a manuscript bearing Sarwani’s name
panels.action: A hand with ink-stained fingers gently closes a worn Persian manuscript, the script on the final page bearing Abbas Khan Sarwani’s name, as lamplight glows over the cover.

dialogue.text: Raisen reminds us that history’s truest honor is not in protecting reputations, but in keeping faith with the record—even when it wounds kings we admire.

i18n.hi: रायसेन हमें याद दिलाता है कि इतिहास की सच्ची इज़्ज़त नाम बचाने में नहीं, रिवायत निभाने में है — चाहे वो उन बादशाहों को ही क्यों न चुभे जिन्हें हम पसंद करते हैं।

subtitle_i18n.en: A king famed for justice faces the one decision his own chronicler could not cleanse.
subtitle_i18n.hi: इंसाफ़ के लिए मशहूर बादशाह, एक ऐसे फ़ैसले के सामने, जिसे उसका इतिहासकार भी साफ़ नहीं कर सका।
